Carbon materials have been widely reported as ESMs/MAMs in recent five years.
The EMI shielding performances of carbon materials are significantly influenced by their nano-structures.
3D carbon materials with films, foams, and aerogels have been considered more promising candidates compared to 1D or 2D materials.
Mesoporous carbon hollow spheres (MCHS) have been synthesized through a hard-template etching method.
The RLmin of MCHS reached -50.9 dB at a thickness of 3.2 mm with a filling ratio of 20 wt%.
The defective onion-like carbon (OLC) displayed effective microwave absorption in the thickness range.
The 3D free-standing graphene foam (GF) exhibited broadband microwave absorption that almost covered the whole 2-18 GHz range.
The defective OLC displayed effective microwave absorption in the thickness range.
The RLmin of the 2D carbon-based nanocomposite supported by metal carbide (CNeFe3C) reached -46.78 dB at 13.53 GHz.
The fe of the 2D carbon-based nanocomposite supported by metal carbide (CNeFe3C) achieved 5.01 GHz with only 10 wt% filling content.
The homemade reduced graphene oxide (rGO) exhibited much higher specific surface area (598 m2/g-1) compared to commercial rGO.
The homemade rGO displayed higher permittivity and larger RL value only at a filling content of 1 wt%.
The nitrogen-doped graphene (NG) exhibited excellent impedance matching and outstanding microwave absorption.
The RLmin of NG reached -50.2 dB at a thickness of 3.2 mm with a filling ratio of 20 wt%.
The fe of NG achieved 5.9 GHz with only 5 wt% filling content.
The RLmin of the HGS@PAC composite reached -32.43 dB at 13.53 GHz with only 10 wt% filling content.
The fe of the HGS@PAC composite achieved 4.2 GHz with only 10 wt% filling content.
